name: Tasha
persona: Seven years of what was on, loved without irony and played on repeat.
blurb: Big pop, chart R&B, top-forty rap and stadium country, played in the car and at the gym. Many plays and few unique tracks, so every pick here is one step sideways rather than five.

lanes.name: Big Pop
lanes.description: The main room: stadium-scale pop albums played front to back and then again.
lanes.arc: The centre of everything for seven years, and still where most of the listening lands.

lanes.name: Chart R&B
lanes.description: Radio R&B and its slower cousins: the songs that carry a whole drive home.
lanes.arc: Grew all summer, mostly at the sadder end and mostly late in the evening.

lanes.name: Top Forty Rap
lanes.description: The rap that reaches the charts: hooks first, features everywhere.
lanes.arc: Steady and enormous, though the newer picks lean further from the singles than they used to.

lanes.name: Stadium Country
lanes.description: Modern country built for arenas, plus the writers quietly doing the real work.
lanes.arc: The clearest riser in the record: barely present in the spring, unavoidable by August.

lanes.name: Gym Hours
lanes.description: Music chosen entirely for tempo: hype rap, big house, anything that helps.
lanes.arc: Perfectly steady, entirely functional, and the highest skip rate in the record by far.

lanes.name: Sad Hours
lanes.description: The other functional lane: quiet pop for the end of a hard day.
lanes.arc: Rises and falls with the month rather than the year, which is the honest shape of it.

lanes.name: Throwback
lanes.description: The pop of a childhood: nineties and two-thousands radio, played without apology.
lanes.arc: Reliable comfort listening, and it spikes every time a new record disappoints.

lanes.name: Latin Pop
lanes.description: Reggaeton and Latin pop, mostly through the crossover hits and increasingly past them.
lanes.arc: Rising fast, and the picks have started moving from the crossovers into the real thing.

lanes.name: K-Pop
lanes.description: The most produced pop on earth, followed properly: b-sides, not just title tracks.
lanes.arc: Went quiet after the spring, which happens when a favourite group stops releasing.

lanes.name: Musicals
lanes.description: The personal outlier: cast recordings, inherited and known by heart.
lanes.arc: Small, constant, entirely unbothered by everything else in the record.

issues.title: First Round
issues.dek: Ten songs from artists you have somehow never played, each one door away from something you play constantly.

issues.title: Sideways Step
issues.dek: The albums three of your favourite singles came from, which you have never opened.

issues.title: Written For You
issues.dek: Every pick this week was written or produced by someone behind a song you already love.

issues.title: Long Way Home
issues.dek: Country has taken over your summer, so this week follows it further in.

issues.title: Loud Room
issues.dek: Gym music with better bones, chosen for tempo and then for quality.

issues.title: Quiet Car
issues.dek: The slow end of pop, and one record that is quieter than anything you own.

issues.title: Old Radio
issues.dek: Two-thousands pop, plus the older records those songs were built out of.

issues.title: Second Chance
issues.dek: You skipped most of last issue, so this one stays closer to home.

issues.title: Curtain Call
issues.dek: Latin pop, a musical, and the best pop record of the year so far.

albums.title: Body Talk
albums.label: Konichiwa
albums.note: The record every crying-on-the-dancefloor song since has been trying to write, and it still outruns all of them.

albums.title: A Seat at the Table
albums.label: Saint
albums.note: Quiet, careful R&B about family and anger, and one of the best-sounding records of the decade.

albums.title: Love Deluxe
albums.label: Epic
albums.note: The most confident quiet record in pop, and the space in it is the whole point.

albums.title: Golden Hour
albums.label: MCA Nashville
albums.note: Country that borrowed disco and daylight, and it won everything for good reason.

albums.title: What's Your Pleasure?
albums.label: PMR
albums.note: A full disco record made with total conviction, and every song is a peak.

albums.title: Heaven or Las Vegas
albums.label: 4AD
albums.note: Vocals used as pure texture over guitars used as light, and it is genuinely soothing.

albums.title: The Velvet Rope
albums.label: Virgin
albums.note: The most personal record a pop star made in the nineties, and the production still sounds current.

albums.title: El Mal Querer
albums.label: Columbia
albums.note: Flamenco rebuilt as pop by someone who studied it properly, and it is thrillingly strange.
albums.why: Flamenco rebuilt as pop by someone who studied it properly, and it is thrillingly strange. You have 512 plays of Rosalía and most of them are the singles; this is the record they came from, with 186.4 hours of Latin Pop in your listening pointing at it. Pitchfork gave it 8.8.

albums.title: Emotion
albums.note: The best pure pop album of its decade, ignored at the time and beloved ever since.
albums.why: The best pure pop album of its decade, ignored at the time and beloved ever since. Big Pop is 612.4 hours of your listening and Sabrina Carpenter alone is 812 plays of it; this is the record that taught that whole lane its manners. Pitchfork scored it 8.2.

critics.title: Butterfly
critics.note: The record where she stopped taking notes from anyone, and the singing is untouchable.

critics.title: Kaleidoscope Dream
critics.note: Radio R&B gone psychedelic at the edges, and Adorn is still one of the great slow-dance singles of its decade.

critics.title: Honey
critics.note: Softer and stranger than her hits, dance music that grieves first and lifts later.

critics.title: Rumours
critics.note: The most-copied breakup album ever made, and every song is somebody's favourite.

critics.title: Whitney Houston
critics.note: The voice every big pop singer since has been measured against, caught right at the start.

critics.title: Take Me Apart
critics.note: R&B stripped to synths and air, sung with the kind of precision that makes quiet sound expensive.

critics.title: Come On Over
critics.note: The best-selling country album in history, and it is a pure pop record wearing a hat.

critics.title: Jolene
critics.note: One quiet little album holds both Jolene and the ballad Whitney later sent into orbit.

critics.title: Off the Wall
critics.note: Disco, funk and pop in one perfectly balanced hour, and nothing has bettered it.

critics.title: Sign o' the Times
critics.note: Funk, gospel, drum machines and prayer across one sprawling double album, played mostly by one man.

critics.title: Back to Black
critics.note: Sixties soul arrangements behind the sharpest lyrics of the century so far.

critics.title: Channel Orange
critics.note: Keyboard soul and patient stories, a writer watching other people's lives with total sympathy.

critics.title: The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill
critics.note: One album, no follow-up, and it still sets the bar for everyone who tries this.

critics.title: Aquemini
critics.note: Southern rap played warm and by hand, live horns under two of the quickest minds ever to share a mic.

critics.title: Supa Dupa Fly
critics.note: Timbaland at his strangest behind the most charismatic rapper of the decade.

critics.title: Late Registration
critics.note: Rap arranged like a film score, strings over soul samples, a big album trying everything at once.

critics.title: Ray of Light
critics.note: A pop star at thirty-nine making the most forward record of her life.

critics.title: The Visitors
critics.note: ABBA at their coldest and saddest, two divorces deep, and the craft never once slips.

critics.title: Hounds of Love
critics.note: Half perfect pop singles, half a suite about drowning, and both halves work.

critics.title: Amor Prohibido
critics.note: The record that made Tejano pop global, sung by someone who made it look effortless.

critics.title: Buena Vista Social Club
critics.note: Havana's old guard playing the songs of their youth in one room, and you can hear how much the room mattered.

critics.title: Barrio Fino
critics.note: The album that carried reggaeton out of San Juan and into everywhere, with Gasolina still the fastest way to start a party.

critics.title: Songs in the Key of Life
critics.note: Two hours of a man at the peak of everything, and not one skippable song.

critics.title: Bad Girls
critics.note: Moroder's machines and a voice that could outrun them, the record where dance music learned to sprint.

critics.title: Discovery
critics.note: The house record that taught pop how to feel joyful, and it has not aged a day.

critics.title: Leak 04-13
critics.note: Bass pushed into the red and hooks half buried, the leak that pop production has chased ever since.

critics.title: West Side Story
critics.note: The score everyone quotes without knowing it, and the cast recording is still the best one.

singles.title: Nasty
singles.note: A whisper over a strut of a beat, R&B that wins by underplaying its hand.

singles.title: Boy's a Liar
singles.note: Two minutes flat, sung like a voice memo over a beat that never raises its voice.

singles.title: Love Me Not
singles.note: Chicago R&B with a voice light enough to float over anything

singles.title: Calm Down
singles.note: Afrobeats built for the exact hour the sun goes down, and it never once pushes.

singles.title: Photo ID
singles.note: Funk-pop with the colour saturation cranked, sung like she is grinning the whole way through.

singles.title: Selfish Soul
singles.note: A violinist who writes hooks, singing about hair like it is the whole argument.

singles.title: Angels in Tibet
singles.note: Accra pop that moves like club music, her feather-light voice riding a beat that never sits still.

singles.title: Go
singles.note: That voice sits so low it reads as a different decade until the drums arrive.

singles.title: Cardboard Box
singles.note: Three voices arranged the way girl groups were arranged in the nineties, on purpose

singles.title: Nike
singles.note: Club pop whispered rather than belted, which turns out to be the harder trick.

singles.title: Moonlight
singles.note: Dreamy, unhurried and romantic, from a singer who makes either language sound like velvet.

singles.title: Blue Lights
singles.note: A debut single that already knew exactly how much space to leave around itself.

singles.title: Persuasive
singles.note: Rap that floats at a murmur, proof that charisma does not need volume.

singles.title: Sunshine
singles.note: Soul with the volume of a kitchen conversation, warm the whole way through.

singles.title: I Want You Around
singles.note: The slow one that everybody plays twice, and the strings do most of the work

singles.title: Sober
singles.note: The kind of breakup song that is embarrassed about itself, which is why it lands.

singles.title: Over
singles.note: New Orleans soul in a modern cut, a can't-quit-you song that glides instead of mopes.

singles.title: Melt
singles.note: Guitar, patience, and a chorus that arrives late enough to feel earned.

singles.title: Hrs and Hrs
singles.note: A first-dance ballad in the old tradition, patient and completely sincere.

singles.title: Boo'd Up
singles.note: A slow burn that took a year to become unavoidable, and then was.

singles.title: Issues
singles.note: She wrote half the songs you already know, and this is the one she kept

singles.title: Chandelier
singles.note: She wrote hits for everyone else first, then kept this one and sang it herself.

singles.title: Habits
singles.note: The messy night sung completely straight, with a chorus big enough to carry it home.

singles.title: American Girl
singles.note: The pen behind a decade of chart pop, taking one swing under her own name.

singles.title: So Hot You're Hurting My Feelings
singles.note: Pop with a strange voice at the centre of it, and the strangeness is the appeal

singles.title: Run Away With Me
singles.note: Opens with a saxophone like a door kicked in, and somehow keeps that up.

singles.title: Hero
singles.note: A big clean-lined ballad from a singer who treats pop melodrama as serious work.

singles.title: Silk Chiffon
singles.note: Pop written by people who clearly love pop, with no apology anywhere in it.

singles.title: Party 4 U
singles.note: Longing set inside a rave, made at home in lockdown and adopted by crowds years later.

singles.title: Free Yourself
singles.note: Disco played straight by someone who spent years being told she was too subtle for it.

singles.title: In Dreams
singles.note: Old-time country sung by someone who actually rode the trains, and it shows

singles.title: I Never Lie
singles.note: Nineties country revived so exactly it feels like a reissue rather than a debut.

singles.title: Welcome to Hard Times
singles.note: Old-fashioned country noir from a Texan who sounds beamed in from a black-and-white matinee.

singles.title: She's Using
singles.note: A murder ballad turned inside out, sung sweetly enough that it takes a verse to notice.

singles.title: Feathered Indians
singles.note: Kentucky songwriting with a voice that has no interest in being polished

singles.title: Jackpot
singles.note: Outlaw country with the swagger intact and none of the costume.

singles.title: Hurtin' on the Bottle
singles.note: Honky-tonk with sawdust on the floor, a drinking song that plays it for truth instead of a wink.

singles.title: Long Hot Summer Day
singles.note: A fiddle, a river, and a band that plays like they have done this a thousand nights.

singles.title: Sleeping on the Blacktop
singles.note: A voice deep as a well over a sparse, stomping blues, cowboy music with the lights off.

singles.title: Please Don't Go
singles.note: Young, plain, and unguarded, which is most of what this corner of country is for.

singles.title: Turn On the Lights again
singles.note: Built out of somebody's voice memo and it still fills a room completely

singles.title: Gosh
singles.note: Built from a rave sample and a lot of restraint, and it still empties the room forward.

singles.title: It Goes Like
singles.note: Piano house straight out of the nineties, sunshine you can set your watch to.

singles.title: Sonder
singles.note: House with a piano player's hands, going somewhere rather than just going.

singles.title: So U Kno
singles.note: Two brothers chopping a soul vocal into a heartbeat, tenderness at running tempo.

singles.title: If U Need It
singles.note: UK garage rebuilt for a generation that never went to the original nights.

singles.title: Holiday
singles.note: Deadpan camp over a filthy house groove, from a band that treats fun as a discipline.

singles.title: Intimidated
singles.note: The drums swing so hard the vocal barely has to try, and it does not.

singles.title: Big Energy
singles.note: Built on the same shimmer as Mariah's Fantasy, rap-pop that walks in already smiling.

singles.title: Baianá
singles.note: Jungle built on a Brazilian sample and a breakbeat that refuses to sit still.

singles.title: Kingston
singles.note: Slide guitar under a pop song, sung like she is barely awake, and it is perfect

singles.title: From the Start
singles.note: Jazz standards rewritten by someone born decades after the standards were.

singles.title: Anything
singles.note: An acoustic guitar, a voice close enough to hear breath, and a love song made of small details.

singles.title: Kill Her Freak Out
singles.note: An organ, a confession, and a title that means exactly what it sounds like.

singles.title: Eugene
singles.note: A diary page set to warm bass and brushed drums, jealousy handled with unusual kindness.

singles.title: Younger & Dumber
singles.note: Starts small and ends up somewhere much louder, without ever changing key.

singles.title: The Perfect Pair
singles.note: A bossa nova sway under bedroom vocals, the gentlest possible way to admit two people are bad for each other.

singles.title: Body
singles.note: One long held thought about leaving, sung at walking pace the entire way.

singles.title: Sexy to Someone
singles.note: Recorded to sound like an old record on purpose, and the songs hold up to it

singles.title: Andromeda
singles.note: Seventies soft rock aimed at the sky, and the reverb is doing real work.

singles.title: Are You That Somebody
singles.note: The strangest drum programming ever to reach number one, and it still sounds like the future

singles.title: Case of the Ex
singles.note: The bassline is the whole song and it knows it, which is why it still works.

singles.title: Full Moon
singles.note: Runs stacked like lacework over clockwork production, the reason singers call her the vocal bible.

singles.title: Foolish
singles.note: A loop lifted from a soul record, sung like a diary entry over the top of it.

singles.title: Fill Me In
singles.note: UK garage smuggled onto pop radio by a teenager, still the smoothest sneaking-around song ever cut.

singles.title: Me & U
singles.note: Almost nothing in the arrangement, and that emptiness is the entire hook.

singles.title: Hit 'Em Up Style
singles.note: Revenge served over a swinging jazz loop, his credit cards footing the bill.

singles.title: Goodies
singles.note: Crunk production under a pop vocal, back when that was a genuinely strange idea.

singles.title: 1 Thing
singles.note: One drum break, one vocal, and one of the great singles of the decade

singles.title: Let Me Love You
singles.note: A ballad engineered so cleanly it has outlived everything around it on the chart.

singles.title: Wild Side
singles.note: A comeback single that bets everything on the dancing, and wins it.
singles.why: A comeback single that bets everything on the dancing, and wins it. SZA, 1,342 plays deep in your record, is the anchor, and this is the same late-night R&B with the lights a little lower.

singles.title: Shea Butter Baby
singles.note: Soul that sounds recorded in one room on a warm afternoon, because it nearly was.
singles.why: Soul that sounds recorded in one room on a warm afternoon, because it nearly was. Your 68.4 hours of SZA are the same register, and you skip her only 12% of the time.

singles.title: ICU
singles.note: A big old-school R&B ballad, no gimmicks, just range and patience.
singles.why: A big old-school R&B ballad, no gimmicks, just range and patience. Summer Walker at 886 plays is the neighbour; this one does not whisper.

singles.title: Good & Plenty
singles.note: Featherweight vocals over chords that keep resolving somewhere unexpected.
singles.why: Featherweight vocals over chords that keep resolving somewhere unexpected. Frank Ocean is 44.2 hours of your life, and this is the same harmonic curiosity with a softer landing.

singles.title: Free Mind
singles.note: A Nigerian voice with enormous patience, and the song never once rushes
singles.why: A Nigerian voice with enormous patience, and the song never once rushes. You have played Frank Ocean 812 times and skip him 9% of the time; this asks for exactly that patience.

singles.title: Flores en Anónimo
singles.note: Bad Bunny's label, a slower cut from the Sauce Boyz sequel, trap drums under a melody that sounds half asleep on purpose.
singles.why: A slower cut from the Sauce Boyz sequel, trap drums under a melody that sounds half asleep on purpose. The door is Rimas Entertainment, Bad Bunny's label: 61.3 hours of it in your listening across 4 artists, and Eladio Carrión has 7 releases there you have never opened.

singles.title: Rush
singles.note: Lagos pop with a hook that flicks like a wrist, easy confidence from a singer barely out of her teens.
singles.why: Lagos pop with a hook that flicks like a wrist, easy confidence from a singer barely out of her teens. Bad Bunny, 1,148 plays on your shelf, is the anchor: same swagger, different coast.

singles.title: Same Room
singles.note: Quiet, close, and unhurried, the sound of somebody thinking out loud.
singles.why: Quiet, close, and unhurried, the sound of somebody thinking out loud. Brent Faiyaz at 748 plays is the nearest thing you own, and this is even quieter.

singles.title: Water
singles.note: The song that carried amapiano's log drums and shakers onto every radio, sung with total cool.
singles.why: The song that carried amapiano's log drums and shakers onto every radio, sung with total cool. Doja Cat, 1,042 plays deep, is the anchor; this has the same ease and none of the jokes.

singles.title: People
singles.note: A question repeated until it stops being small talk and starts being the song.
singles.why: A question repeated until it stops being small talk and starts being the song. It comes through your 48.6 hours of Doja Cat, and it is the sadder room next door.

singles.title: Feliz Cumpleaños Ferxxo
singles.note: Medellín reggaeton gone soft in the middle, a birthday song that plays like a love letter.
singles.why: Medellín reggaeton gone soft in the middle, a birthday song that plays like a love letter. Karol G, 686 plays on your shelf, is the anchor, and this is the same city with a softer voice.

singles.title: Todo de Ti
singles.note: Disco bones under a reggaeton vocal, and it moves like it was built to.
singles.why: Disco bones under a reggaeton vocal, and it moves like it was built to. You have played Bad Bunny 1,148 times and skip him 18% of the time; this is what his radio sounds like between his songs.

singles.title: Classy 101
singles.note: A Puerto Rican newcomer trading verses with Feid, cool as the other side of the pillow.
singles.why: A Puerto Rican newcomer trading verses with Feid, cool as the other side of the pillow. Bad Bunny is 58.6 hours of your life, and this is the next voice out of the same island.

singles.title: Amor Tumbado
singles.note: Corridos rewritten for a much younger room, guitars first and everything else after.
singles.why: Corridos rewritten for a much younger room, guitars first and everything else after. Peso Pluma at 386 plays is the anchor, and this is the record that opened his door.

singles.title: Marchita
singles.note: One voice and one cuatro, recorded close, and it is completely disarming
singles.why: One voice and one cuatro, recorded close, and it is completely disarming. Rosalía, 512 plays deep, is the neighbour; this is the same seriousness with all the production removed.

singles.title: Mafiosa
singles.note: Somewhere between salsa and a threat, delivered with total commitment.
singles.why: Somewhere between salsa and a threat, delivered with total commitment. Your 26.8 hours of Rosalía are the same theatre, and this one bites.

singles.title: She Used to Be Mine
singles.note: She wrote the show and then sang its saddest song better than the cast did.
singles.why: She wrote the show and then sang its saddest song better than the cast did. You have 624 plays of cast recordings and skip them 8% of the time; this is the songwriter stepping out from behind them.

singles.title: Why We Build the Wall
singles.note: Written years before the stage version, and it has only got heavier since.
singles.why: Written years before the stage version, and it has only got heavier since. Your 42.6 hours of cast recordings almost certainly include the show; this is where it started.

singles.title: What He Didn't Do
singles.note: Nashville heartbreak with the details left in, from the label that pressed the country records you still play the most.
singles.why: Nashville heartbreak with the details left in. Big Machine runs 96.2 hours deep in your listening, 6 of its artists in rotation, and Carly Pearce has 3 releases there you have never opened.

singles.title: Snow Angel
singles.note: Came off a Broadway stage and into pop without softening any of the delivery.
singles.why: Came off a Broadway stage and into pop without softening any of the delivery. Ben Platt, 214 plays on your shelf, made the same crossing, and you skip him 15% of the time, so you know the risk.

mixes.note: Radio One's new music flagship, where next spring's choruses turn up before anyone has agreed on them.
The interview show, but the records either side of the talking are the reason to stay
The evening premiere show, big pop treated as news the moment it lands.
R&B radio with a long memory, current names threaded between the ones they grew up on.
The late show, built for driving home, and it never once gets loud
Nashville radio hosted by a songwriter, so the big names arrive with their credits showing.
Peak-time dance radio with no slow patches, exactly the tempo a hard hour asks for.
New York rap radio done properly, with actual opinions between the records
Left-of-centre R&B from a host who hears singers a year before everyone else does.
Jazz-leaning radio from the station Gilles Peterson built, the slow-burning end of the soul you already love.
Daytime pop radio done properly, big records played loud with an actual person between them.
Dance anthems back to back with real glee, radio that assumes you are already moving.
Two hours of reggaeton and its neighbours, sequenced by someone who loves all of it
Pop with its dancing shoes on, hosted like a night out that starts early.

mixes.note: Goyri's three-hour trip through Latin music on KEXP, reggaeton next to cumbia next to whatever came out this week. Bad Bunny is the way in.
mixes.why: Goyri's trip through Latin music on KEXP, Los Fabulosos Cadillacs next to Ed Maverick next to whatever came out this week. 38 tracks, 5 by artists you play and 33 you do not, and Bad Bunny at 1,148 plays is the door.

mixes.note: Western swing from the vaults, the fiddles and steel that the arena names still borrow from. Kacey Musgraves is the closest thing on your shelf.
mixes.why: NTS's Country Hayride given over to western swing, Bob Wills and Spade Cooley, the fiddles and steel the arena names still borrow from. 16 tracks, 2 by artists you play and 14 you have never heard, with Kacey Musgraves at 682 plays as the closest thing on your shelf.

mixes.note: Two hours of tech house built for the last set of the night, or the last set at the gym. Calvin Harris is the name you know; the rest hit harder.
mixes.why: Two hours of tech house built for the last set of the night, or the last set at the gym. 31 tracks, 7 by names you play and 24 you have never heard, and Calvin Harris at 848 plays is the one you know; the rest hit harder.

revivals.title: Cruel Summer
revivals.note: Played more than any other song in your entire listening, and then nothing for a year

revivals.title: Levitating
revivals.note: Disco-pop with springs in its heels, still the easiest yes in her catalogue.

revivals.title: positions
revivals.note: Plucked strings over soft drums, Ariana at her most weightless.

revivals.title: Kill Bill
revivals.note: The song of one whole summer, worn completely smooth and then retired

revivals.title: Girls Need Love
revivals.note: A slow bedroom plea with all the air left in, the song that made understatement her signature.

revivals.title: Pink + White
revivals.note: A warm tumble of piano and strings with Beyonce humming underneath, an album cut people treat like a single.

revivals.title: God's Plan
revivals.note: The friendliest Drake has ever sounded on record, a victory lap you can hum.

revivals.title: Sicko Mode
revivals.note: The gym song for two straight years, and it stopped working all at once

revivals.title: Say So
revivals.note: Roller-rink disco with the guitar doing half the flirting.

revivals.title: Slow Burn
revivals.note: The unhurried opener that sets Golden Hour's whole temperature, country with its shoulders down.

revivals.title: Something in the Orange
revivals.note: A campfire ballad sung close to breaking, heartland heartbreak with no gloss on it.

revivals.title: Tennessee Whiskey
revivals.note: A voice like worn leather over a slow soul sway, the cover that outgrew its original.

revivals.title: Titanium
revivals.note: Sia hitting the chorus like a flare, the template for a decade of arena-sized hope.

revivals.title: Savage
revivals.note: Sparse drums and total command, confidence you can borrow for an hour.

revivals.title: Feels
revivals.note: Sunshine funk-pop with Pharrell at his breeziest, built for open windows.

revivals.title: when the party's over
revivals.note: A song for one specific kind of night, played through a whole year of them

revivals.title: I miss you, I'm sorry
revivals.note: A whispered apology of a song, the diary entry that built her audience.

revivals.title: Mariners Apartment Complex
revivals.note: Lana in warm folk-rock mode, steadier and kinder than her reputation lets on.

revivals.title: Toxic
revivals.note: Surf strings and a spy-film hook, pop engineering that has never dated.

revivals.title: U Got It Bad
revivals.note: The lovesick slow jam other lovesick slow jams measure themselves against.

revivals.title: Love on Top
revivals.note: The key changes that used to get played on every good morning, and not once lately

revivals.title: Desperado
revivals.note: Moody and dusty, built for night highways, proof that Anti runs deeper than its singles.

revivals.title: Tití Me Preguntó
revivals.note: A dembow that keeps changing shape mid-song, mischief with a sad heart underneath.

revivals.title: Provenza
revivals.note: Reggaeton slowed to beach pace, an invitation of a song.

revivals.title: Ditto
revivals.note: Played constantly all spring and then dropped the moment the group went quiet

revivals.title: Feel Special
revivals.note: A comfort anthem under all the gloss, one of K-pop's kindest choruses.

revivals.title: Satisfied
revivals.note: The showstopper that rewinds the wedding to tell the truth about it, rap-speed and heartbroken.

releases.title: The Tortured Poets Department Anthology
releases.note: There will be nothing else on for a fortnight and that is fine.

releases.title: Radical Optimism Deluxe
releases.note: The dance-floor album back with its pockets emptied out.

releases.title: The Giver
releases.note: Chappell goes full country romp, fiddle out front, and it fits her.

releases.title: Guts Spilled
releases.note: Four extra songs and one of them is the best thing she has written.

releases.title: Hit Me Hard and Soft Tour
releases.note: The quietest arena show in pop, finally captured.

releases.title: Punisher Anniversary
releases.note: A reissue with demos, and the demos are somehow sadder.

releases.title: Virgin
releases.note: Lorde stripped back down to nerves and synths.

releases.title: Larger Than Life Deluxe
releases.note: More late-night R&B from the smoothest pessimist working.

releases.title: Beloved
releases.note: That baritone again, set in older and warmer soul arrangements.

releases.title: For All the Dogs Scary Hours
releases.note: Drake rolls his sleeves up for the rap-heavy expansion.

releases.title: Vie
releases.note: Doja pivots again, this time toward gleaming eighties pop.

releases.title: Pink Friday 2 Gag City
releases.note: An extended stay in the pink city her fans dreamed up.

releases.title: Megan Act II
releases.note: A second act for the self-titled album.

releases.title: Funk Wav Bounces Vol. 3
releases.note: A third summer of sunlit funk with a long guest list.

releases.title: Dreamboy
releases.note: The next costume change, worn with total commitment.

releases.title: The Great American Bar Scene
releases.note: Barroom hymns, mostly quiet, occasionally huge.

releases.title: One Thing at a Time Encore
releases.note: An encore for the album that would not leave the charts.

releases.title: Debí Tirar Más Fotos
releases.note: A whole record about missing home, and it is his best in years.

releases.title: Lux
releases.note: Recorded with an orchestra in thirteen languages, apparently.

releases.title: Supernatural
releases.note: The first release since the group went quiet, so this matters.

releases.title: Jump
releases.note: All four back on one track, chorus aimed at stadiums.

releases.title: Cowboy Carter Act III
releases.note: The last part of the trilogy, and the country one was extraordinary.

releases.title: Coming Home Live
releases.note: The homecoming set from a showman who still does it on skates.

catalogs.note: The most-played artist in your listening by a mile, and two whole albums have never been opened.
You play the singles constantly and skip the albums, which she would take personally.

unheard.title: If You're Reading This It's Too Late

catalogs.note: Hundreds of plays and the two records everyone agrees are his best are untouched.
The songs from the album get played and the album never does.
One summer of singles, and the records they came from still sealed.
You know every single and have never sat with either album end to end.
